rawFindings.title: Incorrect instantiation of MultiConfigPath
rawFindings.explanation: The patch replaces the previous usage of `multiConfigPath` as a function to instantiates with `new MultiConfigPath(this)`, but the module `multi_config_path.js` exports a function that returns a function (i.e., it is a factory), not a class constructor. Using `new` here will cause incorrect behavior or runtime error.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the line `var mcp = new MultiConfigPath(this);` to `var mcp = MultiConfigPath(this);` to correctly obtain the multiConfigPath function.

rawFindings.title: Inconsistent usage of MultiConfigPath instance naming
rawFindings.explanation: The code uses `mcp(base, args.config)` but the assigned variable is `mcp` which is created by `new MultiConfigPath(this)` at line 36, which is incorrect as explained above. Even if usage was consistent, the naming `mcp` resembles an instance, but it is a function. Adding clarity by using the original function style improves readability.
rawFindings.suggestion: After fixing the instantiation issue, rename `mcp` to `multiConfigPath` to match original naming or clarify that it is the function returned by the factory.
